tools.name: healthz
tools.description: Returns the upstream API status, environment, and version.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Returns the caller's identity, org, role, role-derived RBAC capabilities, and token scopes. Use this to check whether the current token may perform an action (e.g. config:write) before attempting it.

tools.name: get_setup_progress
tools.description: Read what the workspace has set up with SHIP so far, as the console's setup checklist shows it: up to 13 milestones in three groups, taken in order (get started, make it yours, make it autonomous). `activeGroup` names the group to work on now, and each group carries its own count. Each milestone say

tools.name: get_billing
tools.description: Read the workspace's credit balance by source and expiry, whether a new mission would start now, the per-mission credit ceiling, the project allowance and recent usage. Check it before dispatching work.

tools.name: list_billing_ledger
tools.description: List where the workspace's credits went, newest first: one entry per mission (its start, each further 3 agent-hours, and messages charged before messages became free), per grant, per adjustment and per expiry. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. Owners and admins only.

tools.name: list_credit_offers
tools.description: List what SHIP sells: the credit packs (credits, the tax-inclusive price in US dollars and the price per credit), the monthly plans under `team.plans` (Starter and Scale: each its credits a month, monthly price, price per credit, which credits added on top also cost, and agents at once), the range o

tools.name: start_credit_checkout
tools.description: Opens a payment page and returns its URL. Nothing is charged until the buyer pays on that page. It sells one credit pack, a monthly plan (offer team, with teamPlan starter or scale, a subscription that renews until cancelled), or extra credits for a workspace already on a plan (offer team_credits, f

tools.name: update_team_subscription
tools.description: Change the workspace's monthly plan subscription: plan switches between starter and scale from the next renewal on (nothing is charged or refunded for the current month; passing the current plan drops a waiting switch), or cancelAtPeriodEnd true ends it when the month already paid for ends, false re

tools.name: request_more_credits
tools.description: Ask for more credits for the workspace, saying what they are for. Any member may ask. The answer says who has the request: SHIP for a sponsored or Enterprise workspace, its owners and admins otherwise. A message sent while a request is open joins it.

tools.name: get_notices
tools.description: Read what needs attention in the workspace, critical first: a tracker connection its vendor no longer accepts (missions cannot start or report back until someone reconnects it), or credits running out. Each notice has a stable id and kind, a message and, when the caller can act, an action URL to han

tools.name: dismiss_notice
tools.description: Close a notice for the person this token acts for, as the console's close button does. Only a notice with dismissible: true can be closed (a low balance). It stays closed while its id lasts: a low balance that a top-up ends and a later spend brings back has a new id and shows again. Critical notices

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects accessible to the calling principal. Returns id, slug, name, status, createdAt for each.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Fetch a single project by its UUID. Returns 404 if the project is not in the caller's org.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Change the settings of one project; a field you leave out keeps its value. status paused or archived stops new missions in the project, and active starts them again. autoMerge sets whether SHIP merges a ready pull request by itself. defaultSandboxTemplateId sets the sandbox the agents start in (null

tools.name: start_mission
tools.description: Hand a mission off to the AI agent team. Omit startAt for the default full run (planner first); pass startAt='builder' with a plan to skip straight to coding; pass startAt='reviewer' or startAt='qa' with an existing prNumber to hand off an existing build. Requires the missions:run token scope.

tools.name: create_mission
tools.description: Create the tracker issue AND start the run in one call, for work that has no issue yet. Pass entryStartAt='builder' with an entryPlan to hand over a plan you already wrote; pass entryStartAt='reviewer'/'qa' with entryPrNumber to hand over an existing build — in which case title may be omitted and th

tools.name: set_agents_override
tools.description: Patch one role's harness/model/effort/prompt for a single mission, layered over ship.yml per-field (a role or field this call omits keeps resolving from ship.yml — SHIP-337). Use promptContent or promptPath(+promptRef) to run an ephemeral prompt experiment (spec D9) without committing to the target

tools.name: get_agents_override
tools.description: Read the per-issue agents/baseBranch override record for one mission, or null when unset.

tools.name: send_mission_instruction
tools.description: Tell a mission what to change. Use kind='follow_up' (the default) to ask for a change: the instruction reaches the agents AND dispatches the builder against the mission's open pull request, overriding cached review and QA verdicts. Use kind='note' to record context for whatever runs next without sta

tools.name: clear_agents_override
tools.description: Delete the per-issue agents/baseBranch override — the mission resolves from ship.yml again.

tools.name: list_missions
tools.description: List missions in the caller's accessible projects, newest activity first, with total for paging. Each has issueId, title, activity (what it does now), pipelineProgress, review/check/test state, PR, cost and paused. Archived missions are left out. Requires the missions:read scope.

tools.name: get_mission
tools.description: Fetch one mission. view='summary' (the default, small enough to poll) returns its summary (activity, stage, review/check/test state, PR, paused and pauseSource, cost), its agent runs (sandboxId, role, status, harness, model, cost) and proofRunSandboxId (pass it to list_artifacts as sandboxId for the

tools.name: pause_mission
tools.description: Hold a mission before its next stage. The stage that runs now finishes; no agent is stopped. Use resume_mission to continue. Requires the missions:write scope and a role that can control missions.

tools.name: resume_mission
tools.description: Continue a paused mission. When a checkpoint holds it (get_mission shows pauseSource 'checkpoint:<role>'), this approves that stage's result and starts the next stage. To ask for changes to the result instead, use send_mission_instruction. Requires the missions:write scope.

tools.name: stop_mission
tools.description: Hard-stop a mission: every agent run of it stops and its work in progress is lost. The pull request stays open, and start_mission starts the mission again. To stop one agent run only, use stop_agent_run. Requires the missions:write scope.

tools.name: approve_mission_ceiling
tools.description: A mission that reached its credit limit pauses until a member lets it continue. This raises the mission's limit by one step and runs the stage that stopped again, so it spends credits: ask the person first. Returns the new limit. Answers 409 when the mission is not at its limit. Requires the mission

tools.name: merge_mission
tools.description: Merge the mission's open pull request on GitHub with the repository's own merge method; the mission then becomes done, and the merge cannot be undone from here. Answers 409 with the reason when the pull request cannot merge. On a merge conflict SHIP starts the builder to fix it and merges once the m

tools.name: decline_mission
tools.description: Close the mission's open pull request on GitHub without merging it; the mission becomes declined, and no call here reopens it. Requires the missions:write scope.

tools.name: set_mission_auto_merge
tools.description: Set whether SHIP merges this mission's pull request by itself once the checks, the review and the test pass. The setting is for this mission only and replaces the project's auto-merge for it; get_project shows the project's. While it is on, SHIP merges without asking again. Requires the missions:wri

tools.name: archive_mission
tools.description: Hide a finished mission from list_missions and the board. Nothing else changes: unarchive_mission shows it again. Requires the missions:write scope and the config:write capability (an owner or admin).

tools.name: unarchive_mission
tools.description: Show an archived mission in list_missions and on the board again. Requires the missions:write scope and the config:write capability.

tools.name: set_mission_disposition
tools.description: Record a person's reason for how a mission ended, which the delivery statistics use: product (real work, judged on its merits), probe (a test on purpose), superseded (another mission replaced it: give supersededBy) or takeover (a person finished the work outside SHIP); null clears it. Set it only wi

tools.name: list_scheduled_tasks
tools.description: List recurring agent missions (scheduled tasks) across the caller's accessible projects — schedule, enabled state, and next/last fire time for each. Pass projectId for the tasks of one project.

tools.name: list_scheduled_task_templates
tools.description: Read-only gallery of curated scheduled task templates — a prepared prompt plus a suggested cadence. A template is content, not a code path: pass its key as templateKey on create_scheduled_task for attribution, or copy its prompt/schedule into a hand-written scheduled task.

tools.name: get_scheduled_task
tools.description: Fetch one scheduled task by id: its project, name, prompt, triggers (schedule), labels, template key, skip-if-previous-open setting, enabled state, and next/last run times. An id outside the caller's accessible projects returns not found. For what each fire produced, use list_scheduled_task_runs.

tools.name: create_scheduled_task
tools.description: Create a recurring agent mission. Firing it — on schedule, or immediately via run_scheduled_task — creates an ordinary tracker issue assigned to the agent, which drives a normal pipeline run: a scheduled task is a stored mission request, not a new execution mode. This tool calls the SHIP API, docume

tools.name: update_scheduled_task
tools.description: Patch a scheduled task's name, prompt, schedule, skip-guard, or enabled state — only the fields passed are changed. To change the schedule, set interval/time/timezone together (plus weekday or dayOfMonth as the interval requires). This tool calls the SHIP API, documented at https://letsship.ai/docs/

tools.name: run_scheduled_task
tools.description: Fire a scheduled task immediately, bypassing both its schedule and the skip-if-previous-open guard — an explicit run always creates a new issue even while a prior fire's mission is still open. Requires the pipeline:control capability and, for a token caller, the missions:run scope — the same authori

tools.name: list_scheduled_task_runs
tools.description: Run history for one scheduled task, each row's status (dispatching/dispatched/skipped/failed) and, once its issue exists, the joined mission progress/cost. A 'dispatched' status means the issue was created and the mission started — never that the work succeeded; read the joined mission state for tha

tools.name: delete_scheduled_task
tools.description: Delete a scheduled task and its run history, which no call can bring back. Missions it already started continue. Setting enabled to false stops new runs and keeps the task and its history. Requires the scheduled-tasks:write scope and the config:write capability.

tools.name: list_mcp_servers
tools.description: The MCP servers a project's repository declares in its MCP file (.mcp.json by default), each with its binding: enabled roles, transport, status, approved tools, per-role effective tool counts (null when the server runs inside the sandbox and the role gets every tool it exposes), and the NAMES of the

tools.name: list_mcp_bindings
tools.description: Every MCP server binding across the projects you can see in your org: project, server, transport, status, enabled roles, how it authenticates, and the NAMES of the credential fields set (never values). Use it to find where a credential is used; use list_mcp_servers for one project's full detail.

tools.name: set_mcp_config_path
tools.description: Point the project at the repository file that declares its MCP servers, e.g. .cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json. null restores the default (.mcp.json). The file is read, never edited. When the repository's ship.yml sets mcp.config, that wins and this call is refused (409); list_mcp_servers reports

tools.name: bind_mcp_server
tools.description: Create or update the binding for a server the repository declares. roles is the full set of pipeline roles that may use it (reviewer and qa only ever receive read-only tools, and cannot use a server that runs inside the sandbox). transport: 'remote' (the gateway proxies to the server's URL), 'isolat

tools.name: unbind_mcp_server
tools.description: Delete a binding and its stored credential: no role receives the server from its next run. The repository's MCP file is not changed, so the server can be bound again. Requires config:write.

tools.name: refresh_mcp_server_tools
tools.description: Snapshot the bound server's current tools (with their readOnlyHint / destructiveHint annotations) for approval. Approvals of tools that no longer exist are dropped. The binding must be ready; a server inside the sandbox has no gateway tool list. Requires config:write.

tools.name: start_mcp_server_oauth
tools.description: Begin the OAuth consent for a server bound as remote. Returns an authorizeUrl that a HUMAN must open in a browser signed in to the SHIP console as the same user this token acts for; the provider returns to the console, which stores the credential. The link is single-use and expires (expiresAt). An a

tools.name: list_agent_runs
tools.description: List the agent runs, live and finished, in the caller's accessible projects, newest first. Each run is one agent in its own sandbox. Returns id (the run's sandbox id), issueId, role, harness, status, instance type, and latest CPU/memory/disk metrics. When more runs match, nextCursor is set: pass it

tools.name: get_agent_run
tools.description: Fetch one agent run: its run record, metric series (CPU/mem/disk over time), and the agent session summaries (role, outcome, cost, sessionId). sessions lists every session of the run's role on the mission; runSessionId names this run's own, so read its log and cost from that one.

tools.name: get_agent_run_logs
tools.description: Fetch a session's log content from one agent run. part=session is the agent stream-json (reasoning + tool calls); part=system is the container/runner stdout (clone, dependency install, validation gate, git, callback); part=prompt is the assembled input prompt. The role and sessionId are fields of th

tools.name: watch_agent_run
tools.description: Wait on one agent run and follow what its agent does, instead of polling get_agent_run. The call returns when the run ends, when its mission moves to another stage, or after maxSeconds. While it waits, each agent event (a thought, a tool call, a plan update, an error) is sent as a progress notificat

tools.name: stop_agent_run
tools.description: Stop the agent in one run before it finishes. Its work in progress is lost, and the run's status becomes stopped a few seconds later. Needs an org admin and the sandboxes:stop scope. This stops one agent run, not the mission: to stop the whole mission, use POST /v1/missions/{issueId}/stop.

tools.name: list_sandbox_templates
tools.description: List the org's sandboxes (definitions agents start in), with each one's active version, size and latest build status.

tools.name: get_sandbox_capacity
tools.description: How many agents the org's missions are running at once against its limit (null while the org is unclassified), which missions wait for an agent slot and why, and whether every slot on the platform is taken. Read from the platform's once-a-minute capacity check.

tools.name: list_sandbox_starters
tools.description: Ready-made sandbox definitions (Python, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby) to create a sandbox from.

tools.name: list_sandbox_template_versions
tools.description: Every saved version of a sandbox, newest first, with the active one marked and each one's latest build.

tools.name: get_sandbox_build_log
tools.description: A page of a build's log after sequence number `after`. Call again with after = nextAfter until done is true.

tools.name: save_sandbox_template
tools.description: Create a sandbox (omit templateId) or change one. A definition is Dockerfile steps on the platform base (RUN, ENV, ARG, WORKDIR, USER; no FROM). A changed definition or size becomes a new version and is built at once; the response carries that build. Refusals name the line or the size bound.

tools.name: activate_sandbox_template_version
tools.description: Make a version the one missions use from their next dispatch. It is rebuilt only if its snapshot is gone; the response says which.

tools.name: build_sandbox_template
tools.description: Build the sandbox's active version, or return the build already running for it.

tools.name: list_sandbox_registries
tools.description: The org's private package registries sandboxes install from: host, auth scheme, username. Never the secret.

tools.name: save_sandbox_registry
tools.description: Store (or replace) the credential for a registry host. The platform attaches it to sandbox requests for that host only; it never enters a sandbox and is never returned.

tools.name: delete_sandbox_template
tools.description: Delete a sandbox with all its versions and builds. Answers 409 while an agent or a project's default sandbox uses it: point those at another sandbox first (update_project with defaultSandboxTemplateId). Missions that run in it now finish. Requires the agents:write scope and the config:write capabili

tools.name: delete_sandbox_registry
tools.description: Delete the stored credential of a private registry (an id from list_sandbox_registries). A sandbox build that installs from that host then gets no credential. Requires the connectors:write scope and the config:write capability.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: List per-mission preview environments for the caller's accessible projects. Returns id, issueId, projectId, prNumber, workerName, and lifecycle status.

tools.name: get_environment
tools.description: Fetch one preview environment's registry row (status, worker name, timestamps).

tools.name: destroy_environment
tools.description: Request teardown of a preview environment (its deployed Worker(s) + every provisioned datastore). Enqueues to the orchestrator; requires project write capability.

tools.name: list_artifacts
tools.description: List proof-of-work artifacts (QA screenshots/video/traces) for the caller's accessible projects. Each row carries kind, content type, caption, the acceptance criterion it proves, the sandboxId of the agent run that produced it, and a long-lived signed serving url. Filter by issueId to get one ticket

tools.name: get_artifact
tools.description: Fetch one artifact's metadata + a long-lived signed serving url (open it to view the screenshot/video).

tools.name: inspect_mission
tools.description: Fetch the typed platform-inspection report for a mission, by its issue id. Returns per-section KV/D1/R2 state: task state, retry reason, dispatch error, latest review + QA verdicts, run index, per-attempt provenance, running sandboxes, and session-log heads. Requires the inspect:read scope.

tools.name: list_orgs
tools.description: List every organization on the platform with its owner email, member count, and pending invite status. Requires platform-admin (cross_org) access.
